newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks make rights progress, but not enough - group.
newsitem.headline: Turks make rights progress, but not enough - group.

text.p: A leading international rights group said in a statement on Thursday that it welcomed recent steps by Turkey to improve its rights record, but said the new measures did not go far enough.

"Human Rights Watch/Helsinki is encouraged by a November 27, 1996 bill the government of Turkey submitted to parliament reducing periods of pre-trial detention (for criminal suspects)," the statement said.

Under the bill the the maximum time a suspect may be held before being charged, and having guaranteed access to a lawyer, will be reduced from 30 days to 10 in the nine emergency rule provinces of the southeast and from two weeks to one in the rest of the country.
But the group said that the bill should guarantee suspects' right to see a lawyer from the time of detention.
Human rights activists say that that the initial period of detention is when suspects are most at risk from torture. Activists say this is systematic in Turkey.

The European Parliament has blocked millions of dollars of aid to Turkey, partly as result of its human rights record. Turkey's new Islamist government's efforts to clean up this record have so far met with little success.
